Question: Another major jolt for Rahul Gandhi as Ashok Chavan, former CM of Maharashtra has quit Congress. What’s your take on this?
Answer: Yes this is the latest news from Maharashtra that Ashok Chavan has quit from the party and he has already sent his resignation letter to the party President Nana Patole. Many top congress leaders are quitting their party when Rahul is dreaming of becoming the next PM. What will happen to his dynastic politics if the trend continues. Already Opposition Alliance is crumbling down as Mamata, Kejriwal, Pinarayi Vijayan are opposed to Congress alliance in their respective states by refusing to seat adjustment proposal. Already Nitish Kumar has quit INDIA Alliance and joined NDA. Madhya Pradesh, UP, Maharashtra and Bihar have substantial number of Loksabha seats which can bring Modi to power. It looks Modi Tsunami has begun and congress is blotting out by the Modi wave.

Name: Gaja Vasisht
Question: Why did Nitish Kumar Bihar CM suddenly removed Lalan Singh from JDU as the party president and he himself has taken over forcefully?
Answer: Lalan Singh was increasingly got identified with Fodder Scandal dynasty family of jailed Lalu Prasad. This closeness with RJD forced Nitish to remove from the party post on the advice of senior party leaders. Nitish was dreaming of becoming the next PM, unfortunately he was ignored by Sonia’s Congress party and this made Nitish change his mind as the entire INDIA Block started distancing itself from Nitish. Lalu too was ignored by the INDIA Block for the reason Rahul Gandhi was not the fit candidate for PM. Lalu was demanding ten Loksabha seats for congress in the next elections and this illogical proposal was rejected by the Leftist and others. There are Forty Loksabha seats in Bihar and if ten seats are given to congress, what about communist because Lalu was demanding twenty five seats for RJD. Lalan Singh was contemplating to break JDU and merge it was RJD since Nitish has only 38 seats. If Nitish is thrown out RJD plus Congress plus Leftists can form the government without Nitish. This is the reason why Lalan Singh was removed. BJP has 78 seats in Bihar Assembly against this RJD has 79 seats. Communists have 16 seats as against this Congress has 19 seats. Nitish is trying to negotiate with BJP by breaking the alliance with RJD. Out of 243 seats to form the government they require 122 seats and if Nitish joins BJP NDA alliance he can easily form the government. But BJP is not trusting Palturam anymore. BJP is very optimistic now about their strength after Lord Shri Ram Temple inauguration as they expect Bihari voters may trounce Nitish and other parties on its own strength this time. Nitish Kumar’s political life may be nearing as the earth is collapsing under his feet since the fight is between RJD and the BJP without unpopular Nitish and Lalu. The same problem is prevailing in Karnataka between Siddaramaiah and DKSHI and let’s see the most interesting political landscape in the coming days.

Name: Gaja Vasisht
Question: How do you describe the tragedy of being Maneka Gandhi and Varun Gandhi in relation to Indira Gandhi, Sonia and BJP denying Lok Sabha ticket to Varun this time?
Answer: It is really sad to describe the unfortunate fate and events which has unfolded in the lives of Maneka Gandhi and her only son Varun Gandhi. When Sanjay Gandhi died in an aircraft crash in 1980 Varun Gandhi was just three months old. Sanjay wanted to be a great politician like his mother. Look at the fate when Sanjay wanted to be a politician his brother Rajiv Gandhi who wanted to be a pilot but, not interested to be a politician like his mother. What happened after is something baffling to us. Sanjay died in that aircraft crash and Rajiv was assassinated as a politician. Both perished leaving their families with tragedies which could not be reconciled with any predictions or explanations. After Sanjay’s death Indira wanted to bring Maneka into politics as she was close to her. However, that dream of bringing Maneka into politics was shattered when Sonia entered the scene. Sonia influenced her mother in law and prevented Maneka from being involved in politics as she pressurised Indira to give ticket to her husband Rajiv from Amethi constituency. Amethi is the constituency of Sanjay Gandhi. After the death of Sanjay Maneka and her son Varun lived with Indira Gandhi’s official residence when she was the PM. Gradually, Sonia influenced Indira to eject Maneka from the residence. One fine day Maneka was asked to get out of the house and Maneka was forced out along with her son Varun who was just five or six months baby. Maneka floated her own party called Sanjay Vichar Manch but, it flopped. She joined VP government and then BJP and got elected to parliament and became minister. Sonia continued to ignore her. Varun is a good politician and he speaks far better than Rahul Gandhi and he is also very popular in UP politics. He is elected from Pilibhit from 2009, 2014 and 2019. However the problem with Varun is that he is very ambitious and wants to become UP CM but, Modi is against this idea. So, Varun is speaking against Modi and Yogi and this has resulted in denying the ticket for his next term. It is also reported that Varun is in contact with Priyanka. His mother Maneka has been given ticket from Sultanpur constituency.

Question: Mamata Didi of TMC and CM of West Bengal has proposed Mallikarjun Kharge’s name for the PM post for the next elections. How do you feel about this proposal?
Answer: It is a googly from Mamata and Kejriwal to Sonia Gandhi. No doubt that the googly is perfect but, let’s see how it may turn out to be in the interest of opposition parties. Just recently Mamata was in Delhi and she had one to one meeting with Kejriwal. After this meeting, Mamata came out with the proposal of Kharge as the face of PM. I think this is a well articulated way of stumping Sonia Gandhi’s dream of projecting her son, the clown prince as the next PM. The moment this news came, Lalu Prasad reacted alongside Nitish Kumar as well. Both of them have refused to this proposal of Kharge as the next PM. It is important to remember that Lalu wants Nitish to move out of Bihar so that his son to be the next CM of Bihar. However, if Kharge’s name is proposed then Nitish will be stuck in Bihar politics without moving out to Delhi. For Kejriwal and Mamata there are substantial Dalit Votes in both Delhi and West Bengal and there’s a fear for them that Modi may snatch away these Dalit Votes in his favour and keeping this basic idea in their mind Kejri and Didi have come out with this proposal in order to save themselves from the BJP. Secondly not all the other opposition leaders are happy with this proposal either because Kharge himself cannot get votes as he is not a national leader and moreover it is impossible that every Dalit will vote enmasse in favour of Kharge as Dalits are not united. Kharge is aged as he is 82 years old. His Hindi is mixture of “Karburgi Urdu” since he hails from Muslims dominated region. He is not popular in Karnataka and this is the very reason that he was not given CM post in the past though he is the senior most congress leader. There’s another important reason and that is Sonia Gandhi wants her son to contest from Karnataka in the next Loksabha elections and Kharge to be contesting from UP since Sonia wants to fill the vacant place left by Mayawati of BSP. This proposal is given by the election strategist Sunil Kanugolu. It is believed that Modi may find it tough to fight against the Dalit Leader Kharge if his name is proposed. However, Modi very popular among the young voters of India though he is Seventy plus and Kharge may not be liked by the younger generation. Lastly Sonia Gandhi at any cost wants her son to be the next PM and this is not acceptable to many opposition leaders because he is incompetent and he has already proved it amply on international level. The moment this news came out Kharge himself has not agreed to such a proposal as he has stated that “FIRST LET US WIN THE ELECTION AND THEN THINK BOUT IT LATER WHEN WE GET THE REQUIRED MAJORITY.

Question: Did you vote today? If so, what is your experience when you visited your voting booth in Bangalore?
Answer: Today morning around 07.15 am I along with my wife went to voting booth in Booth No.16, St. Anne’s School premises next to Ulsoor Police Station, Bangalore. Fortunately I was able to vote within 20 minutes or so. The police directed all the voters to switch off their phones and leave them outside the polling booths. I asked the police to provide alternate queue to senior citizens, but he said that there’s insufficient space to accommodate another queue for seniors. Before we enter the booth we are told to stand in the queue without fans and no water to drink as they have made no provision for such simple things for the poor voters. I saw only senior citizens who were standing in the queue, but not our youngsters. After coming out I saw the other Booths with long queues and the aged, senior citizens were standing in the queue waiting for their turn. I was sad that Election Commission of India is incompetent to handle such simple things and provide minimum facilities of the voters who are made to vote under gruelling conditions. Why can’t the media and the TV channels show this to our PM, EC and the Supreme Court and expose the truth.
